channel.title: NPR Topics: Economy
channel.description: Understand the economic forces shaping daily life. Follow NPR for stories on inflation, affordability, consumer spending and jobs, plus episodes of Planet Money and The Indicator.

item.title: From Wall Street to Main Street, how artificial intelligence is affecting the economy
item.description: Artificial intelligence is sending shock waves through the stock market, as investors try to predict how their big bets will pay off. Meanwhile some real businesses are putting AI to work, with mixed results.
item.content:encoded: Artificial intelligence is sending shock waves through the stock market, as investors try to predict how their big bets will pay off. Meanwhile some real businesses are putting AI to work, with mixed results.
item.dc:creator: Scott Horsley

item.title: Chief economist for Moody's Analytics on why Anthropic's IPO caused market volatility
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Mark Zandi, chief economist for Moody's Analytics, about Anthropic's Wall Street debut and why it seems to have triggered recent market volatility.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Mark Zandi, chief economist for Moody's Analytics, about Anthropic's Wall Street debut and why it seems to have triggered recent market volatility.
item.dc:creator: Michel Martin

item.title: AI is making it hard for young people to find work, report says
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Matt Sigelman, president of the Burning Glass Institute, about a new report indicating that AI is already squeezing the job market for young jobseekers.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Matt Sigelman, president of the Burning Glass Institute, about a new report indicating that AI is already squeezing the job market for young jobseekers.

item.title: Rising costs leave consumers looking for Thanksgiving bargains
item.description: It's Thanksgiving week and you may have seen that turkey and gravy are more expensive. NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, about why costs are up.

item.title: He expected a small-business loan. He got a 7-year nightmare
item.description: America's fastest-growing source of funding for small businesses is also one of the least regulated. One man has waged a long, lonely fight to recoup its punishing cost.

item.title: What's next after a brutal stock plunge we might have seen coming
item.description: Stocks tanked this week as investors grew wary of tech investments that have seen years of growth. NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Katie Martin of the Financial Times about the global ripple effects.

item.title: Just how vulnerable are we to cyberattacks?
item.description: In a week of outages, we're thinking about the rising threat of AI-powered cyberattacks. But sometimes, it's not the most sophisticated attack that's concerning, but the easy targets buried in old software.

item.title: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow?
item.description: In late October, Google had the worst stock day in its history as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter asks: has Google been caught in "the innovator's dilemma"?

item.title: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
item.description: While the rise of AI continues to fuel the debate over whether college is worth the cost, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment, drawing in people of all backgrounds including college graduates.

item.title: Does Europe regret its bet on U.S. defense?
item.description: Europe bet big on American defense technology and they're now paying the price. Years-long backlogs are underway due to production delays and the U.S. own military needs.
